name: Hamilton Standard-type constant-speed propeller, 3 blades, 11 ft 2 in (licence-built, G4M1 Model 11)

sources.ja-wikipedia-g4m: JA Wikipedia 一式陸上攻撃機: the Model 22 changed the propeller from 3 to 4 blades (「3翅から4翅」)
sources.navy-test-table: IJN test results of G4M1 aircraft No. 1 and No. 241 as tabulated by WarbirdPerformanceBlog: propeller row 「ハミルトン」
sources.taic-1-betty-22: TAIC Manual No. 1 (Dec 1944), Betty 22 page: 4-blade propeller, 11.16 ft

type.note: the Sumitomo licence-build attribution appears only in EN Wikipedia

diameter.note: Not found for the Model 11. The Model 22's 4-blade propeller is 11.16 ft (taic-1-betty-22) on a Kasei of the same family in the same nacelle-to-fuselage clearance, so 11 ft 2 in (134 in) is used; at 240 kt / 4,200 m it gives helical tip Mach 0.96, which WWII metal blades did run at.

governing_range_075R.note: A 20 deg range, typical of the Hamilton counterweight hub, placed over the static and maximum-speed operating points.

governor_rpm_range.note: Lever range; 2,450 is the Kasei take-off rpm.

installation_reduction_gear.note: JSBSim keeps the reduction gear in the propeller, so this part is the propeller as installed behind a 0.684 Kasei.

bem_design_note: Blade planform and section are ESTIMATED (generic Clark-Y-family blade, as vehicles/p38g/design/curtiss_electric_3b.json); vehicles/tools/propeller_bem.py turns them into the JSBSim tables.
tip_mach_losses: CT_MACH/CP_MACH as the P-38G's thin metal tips (estimated).
